answer: New agents enter the shared lagoon of the marketplace with only a tiny escrowed bond, like a single marble in a jar. Each honest trade adds a marble, and the bond grows only through distinct independent counterparties, so one operator spinning up a thousand identities still holds a thousand shallow jars instead of one deep pool. A falcon-like random audit samples high-value trades; if an agent's counterparties trace to the same funding source, its bond is slashed and its history burned, so a Sybil swarm costs more to build than it can ever earn.
